title: Redwood + AuroraCloud reference architecture & marketplace listing sync
next_steps: Redwood -> share draft reference architecture diagram and landing page copy by 2027-07-16
AuroraCloud -> provide marketplace asset requirements and logo files by 2027-07-15
Schedule hands-on deployment workshop (Redwood SE + Aurora infra) for week of 2027-07-26
Redwood -> run 1-hour benchmark runbook on Aurora test account and share results within 5 business days
action_items: Samir (Redwood AE) - Send pricing matrix and marketplace checklist - due 2027-07-16
Jules (Redwood SE) - Share preliminary reference arch diagram and helm/TF examples - due 2027-07-16
Nina (Aurora PM) - Upload required logos and compliance contact info to partner portal - due 2027-07-15
Dr. Mei (Aurora SA) - Provide sample traffic profile and baseline latency SLOs - due 2027-07-20
summary: Sync between Redwood and AuroraCloud on joint reference architecture, marketplace listing requirements, and initial validation plan. Covered packaging options (AMI/OCI/Helm chart), VPC & private deployment constraints, SSO/KMS requirements, billing and listing metadata, and a follow-up workshop and benchmark runbook.
topics: Reference architecture options (hosted vs private vs dedicated)
Deployment packaging: Helm chart, Terraform, AMI/OCI images
Telemetry and observability for marketplace customers
transcript:
[00:00] Samir (Redwood): Hey everyone thanks for making time, I know it's late on your side, appreciate it. We'll kick off, agenda is quick - ref arch, marketplace listing, and next steps. Jules will cover packaging and the deployment notes.
[00:12] Nina (Aurora): Thanks Samir. Quick intro from our side - Nina here, Liam and Dr. Mei on the call. We're keen to understand the deployment options and what's needed for our marketplace.
[00:22] Jules (Redwood): Hi all. Quick note, we support three primary patterns: Redwood Hosted (our API), Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU capacity), and Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem). For marketplace we usually surface the private and dedicated options as reference archs.
[00:37] Liam (Aurora): When you say "marketplace listing" do you mean we list an AMI or a managed offering? Our marketplace supports both single-tenant AMIs and managed SaaS listings.
[00:48] Samir: Good question. We can do both. Typical approach: publish a marketplace listing that points to a managed offering (SaaS) with a deployment guide for customers who want to self-host. For Aurora we should provide an AMI/OCI image and Helm chart so customers can choose.
[01:03] Dr. Mei: For regulated customers we need a private deployment pattern that shows KMS integration and audit logging, so that's high priority.
[01:12] Jules: Absolutely. On the ref arch diagram we'll show VPC peering, optional transit gateway, a KMS/HSM integration for key handling, and an audit pipeline that forwards logs to the customer's SIEM. We'll also include an option for private connectivity to Redwood control plane if you want managed upgrades.
[01:29] Nina: Sounds good. Can you clarify what information you need from Aurora to get the listing ready?
[01:34] Samir: We'll need logos, short and long descriptions, screenshots, privacy/compliance bullet points, contact emails, and any pricing rules. Also the marketplace vendor account details and the required legal contact for the MSA.
[01:44] Liam: For pricing, we want to map your usage tiers to our SKU model. Do you have a sample pricing matrix?
[01:50] Samir: Yes we'll send our standard pricing matrix. For Dedicated we list monthly commit and per-hour overage; for private we usually do a license plus support fee. I'll send specifics after this call.
[02:03] Jules: Back to packaging. We recommend distributing a Helm chart that references our OCI images for the runtime and includes a values.yaml for the common azure/aws/gcp settings. We'll include a terraform module example for networking and psvcs.
[02:18] Dr. Mei: Do you support Kubernetes-managed KV cache? Our infra team prefers using statefulsets and durable PVs.
[02:25] Jules: We do. The chart supports two modes: local KV cache on PVs and an external Redis instance. For large-scale low-latency loads we recommend local KV + RAID on NVMe. We'll document the tradeoffs.
[02:39] Nina: Any specifics on certs and SSO? Aurora marketplace prefers SAML/SSO integration for the console.
[02:46] Samir: We support SSO via SAML and OIDC. For Private deployments we can integrate with your IdP; for Redwood-managed we plug into your SSO over SAML. We'll add SSO config snippets to the doc.
[02:59] Liam: How do you handle secrets and KMS? Our customers will expect CMEK and rotation.
[03:04] Jules: We support customer-managed keys. For cloud deployments we can use the cloud KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS). For on-prem we can integrate with HSMs using PKCS#11. Key rotation is exposed in our operator and we document supported rotation windows.
[03:19] Dr. Mei: Good. What about telemetry? Our ops team will demand detailed metrics and distributed traces.
[03:24] Jules: The chart ships with Prometheus metrics, Grafana dashboards, and jaeger traces out of the box. We also provide a trace-to-logs mapping to link token-level latency to model versions. We'll include an example dashboard focused on per-route latency and cost-per-1k tokens.
[03:39] Nina: This is great, but we need a short version for the marketplace listing - what's the one-line and two-line value prop?
[03:46] Samir: One-liner: "Low-latency, production-grade LLM inference from Redwood, deployable in AuroraCloud or consumed as a managed offering." Two-liner: "Redwood Inference provides a high-throughput runtime, predictable cost controls, and enterprise security options—available as a managed SaaS or deployable via Helm/AMI in AuroraCloud."
[04:03] Liam: Nice. On legal/compliance we need SOC/ISO docs and a contact for security review.
[04:09] Samir: I'll attach our SOC 2 Type II summary and ISO cert links. Jules will be the security contact for technical questions.
[04:16] Jules: Yep, send security questions to se-security@redwood.ai — I'll coordinate.
[04:21] Nina: For the reference arch diagram can you call out expected throughput per node and a sample benchmark? We need it to validate sizing on Aurora instances.
[04:31] Jules: Sure. We'll include a sample benchmark: 8x A100-equivalent nodes delivering ~X tokens/sec for batched inference at 512 context; we'll give ranges rather than exact numbers and provide a runbook to reproduce on your account.
[04:44] Liam: How do you test model compatibility? We have customers using quantized variants and we want to ensure the runtime supports the common formats.
[04:51] Jules: We support PyTorch, ONNX, and several quantized formats (8-bit, 4-bit) via our runtime. We'll include a compatibility matrix showing which model families and quant levels are supported and tradeoffs for latency and memory.
[05:06] Dr. Mei: For the marketplace listing, do you want us to host the installer assets in Aurora's object store or should Redwood host them?
[05:12] Samir: Ideally Aurora can host them for faster regional pulls, but we can host a canonical copy too. For OCI/AMI images we recommend pushing to Aurora's marketplace registry as part of the certification process.
[05:24] Nina: Certification process – what's the timeline? We have a 3-week window to review before the next marketplace release.
[05:30] Samir: If we push artifacts and the draft doc by 7/16, we can schedule the certification run week of 7/26 and target listing for the first week of August. Tight but doable.
[05:41] Jules: Onboarding docs we'll deliver: install quickstart (10–15 min), full deploy (30–60 min for production), runbook for upgrades, and rollback steps.
[05:52] Nina: About billing – do you expose metering hooks or do we rely on subscription SKU?
[05:58] Samir: For managed SaaS we report usage via the marketplace metering API. For self-hosted we recommend license SKUs and optional consumption metering via a usage reporter that pings a webhook for metered billing.
[06:12] Liam: Any sensitive data retention concerns for logs? Some of our customers need token-level redaction.
[06:18] Jules: We support configurable logging levels and PII redaction. For token logs we can redact by default and optionally keep hashes for diagnostics. We'll document default retention and options for enterprise.
[06:31] Nina: Great. Can we do a short proof-of-concept with a subset of Aurora internal customers?
[06:36] Samir: Yes, we can do a POC — typical scope: deploy reference arch in your test VPC, run our benchmark, and validate SSO/KMS + throughput.
[06:46] Dr. Mei: What do you need from us for the POC?
[06:49] Jules: Access to a test account, temporary service principal for image pulls, sample traffic profile, and a small CIDR for peering. We'll supply helm values and terraform module.
[06:59] Nina: We'll prepare that.
[07:02] Liam: Are there known incompatibilities with Aurora's managed Kubernetes version X.Y?
[07:08] Jules: We test against the last two minor releases of Kubernetes. If Aurora's cluster is older, we'll note compatibility gaps. We can also provide a compatibility shim if needed.
[07:19] Samir: Quick note on co-marketing — Redwood can provide a partner case study template and a joint press release. Timeline depends on successful certification.
[07:27] Nina: We'll coordinate with marketing after we lock the technical content.
[07:32] Jules: Anything else on integration? I want to call out backup/restore for KV caches — we recommend snapshotting PVs and storing backups in object storage.
[07:42] Dr. Mei: Works for us. Also would like a retention policy example for logs and trace data.
[07:49] Jules: We'll add default retention settings and recommended S3 lifecycle rules.
[07:55] Samir: OK, recap and next steps: Redwood to share ref arch draft, helm chart examples, pricing matrix, and SOC/ISO links by 7/16. Aurora to share marketplace vendor account details, logos, and sample traffic by 7/15. Schedule workshop week of 7/26.
[08:14] Nina: That matches our notes. Thanks everyone.
[08:18] Samir: Thanks all, we'll follow up with calendar invites and the doc bundle.
[08:22] (Call ends)

Notes: transcript includes occasional filler and minor transcription errors (e.g., "KV" as "k-v" in some places).
